### Module 03 — Hypothesis Testing for Health Outcomes

# Hypothesis Testing for Health Outcomes

***
**Learning objectives**
- Select the right test for continuous, categorical, and count outcomes
- Apply chi-square, Fisher's exact, t-test, and ANOVA in clinical contexts
- Interpret p-values, effect sizes, and confidence intervals correctly
- Correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)
- Distinguish statistical significance from clinical significance

**Estimated time:** 2 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `stats`, `broom`, `patchwork`

## 1. Setup & Dataset

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(patchwork)
library(tibble)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Synthetic clinical dataset ────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1000
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)

ages     <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers   <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03)
)
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges  <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)

set.seed(99)
diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
hypertension  <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.7 * base[, 1] - 0.2))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] + 0.5 * hypertension - 1.5))
readmitted_30 <- rbinom(
  N, 1,
  logistic(-2.5 + 0.4 * heart_failure + 0.3 * diabetes + 0.2 * (los_days > 7))
)
admit_type <- sample(
  c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02)
)

set.seed(21)
glucose    <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 105 + 15 * diabetes, 28), 50), 400), 1)
creatinine <- round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 1.6 + 0.8 * heart_failure, scale = 0.6), 0.4), 10), 2)
hba1c      <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 6.5 + 0.8 * diabetes, 1.4), 4), 14), 1)
sbp        <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 128 + 12 * hypertension, 18), 80), 200), 0)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  admit_type    = admit_type,
  los_days      = los_days,
  total_charge  = charges,
  diabetes      = diabetes,
  hypertension  = hypertension,
  heart_failure = heart_failure,
  readmitted_30 = readmitted_30,
  glucose       = glucose,
  creatinine    = creatinine,
  hba1c         = hba1c,
  sbp           = sbp
) |>
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "Dataset: %d x %d  |  Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
  nrow(df), ncol(df), mean(df$readmitted_30) * 100
))
print(summary(df |> select(where(is.numeric))))
```

## 2. Test Selection Framework

```
Outcome type?
├── Categorical (proportions) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── 2 groups, expected counts ≥5 → Chi-square test
│     ├── 2 groups, small N or sparse cells → Fisher's exact test
│     └── >2 groups → Chi-square (or log-linear model)
│
├── Continuous, 2 groups ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── Check normality (Shapiro-Wilk n<50, D'Agostino n≥50)
│     │     ├── Normal + equal variance → Independent samples t-test
│     │     ├── Normal + unequal variance → Welch's t-test
│     │     └── Non-normal (LOS, charges) → Mann-Whitney U
│     └── Paired / matched → Paired t-test (normal) or Wilcoxon signed-rank
│
├── Continuous, >2 groups ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── Normal + equal variance → One-way ANOVA + post-hoc Tukey HSD
│     └── Non-normal → Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn's test
│
└── Count / rate outcome → Poisson test or negative binomial
```

## 3. Normality Assessment

```{r}
# D'Agostino-Pearson analogue: moments test via Pearson's chi-square of skew + kurtosis
dagostino_pearson <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m3 <- mean((x - mean(x))^3)
  m4 <- mean((x - mean(x))^4)
  s  <- sd(x)
  skew <- m3 / s^3
  kurt <- m4 / s^4 - 3
  z_skew <- skew / sqrt(6 / n)
  z_kurt <- kurt / sqrt(24 / n)
  stat <- z_skew^2 + z_kurt^2
  p <- pchisq(stat, df = 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
  list(statistic = stat, p.value = p)
}

normality_report <- function(series, name) {
  s <- series[!is.na(series)]
  skewness <- mean((s - mean(s))^3) / sd(s)^3
  if (length(s) < 50) {
    sw <- shapiro.test(s)
    stat <- unname(sw$statistic)
    p <- sw$p.value
    test_name <- "Shapiro-Wilk"
  } else {
    dp <- dagostino_pearson(s)
    stat <- dp$statistic
    p <- dp$p.value
    test_name <- "D'Agostino"
  }
  normal <- p > 0.05
  cat(sprintf(
    "  %-20s: skew=%+.2f | %s p=%.4f → %s\n",
    name, skewness, test_name, p,
    if (normal) "NORMAL" else "NON-NORMAL"
  ))
  normal
}

cat("Normality assessment:\n")
norm_results <- list()
for (pair in list(
  c("age", "Age"), c("los_days", "LOS"), c("total_charge", "Charge"),
  c("glucose", "Glucose"), c("creatinine", "Creatinine"), c("sbp", "SBP")
)) {
  col <- pair[[1]]; label <- pair[[2]]
  norm_results[[col]] <- normality_report(df[[col]], label)
}

cat("\nDecision summary:\n")
for (col in names(norm_results)) {
  rec <- if (norm_results[[col]]) "→ Use t-test / ANOVA" else "→ Use Mann-Whitney / Kruskal-Wallis"
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: %s\n", col, rec))
}
```

## 4. Chi-Square & Fisher's Exact Tests (Categorical Outcomes)

```{r}
# ── 4.1  Chi-square: sex × readmission ───────────────────────────────────────
ct <- table(df$sex, df$readmitted_30)
ct_m <- addmargins(ct)
cat("Contingency table — Sex × 30-day readmission:\n")
print(ct_m)

chi <- chisq.test(ct)
cramer_v <- sqrt(unname(chi$statistic) / (nrow(df) * min(nrow(ct) - 1, ncol(ct) - 1)))
cat(sprintf("\nChi-square: χ²=%.3f, df=%d, p=%.4f\n",
            unname(chi$statistic), chi$parameter, chi$p.value))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (Cramér V): %.3f\n", cramer_v))
cat(sprintf("Minimum expected count: %.1f (>5 = chi-square is appropriate)\n",
            min(chi$expected)))
```

```{r}
# ── 4.2  Fisher's exact: small-cell scenario ─────────────────────────────────
# Rare outcome: heart failure among Newborn admissions
rare_ct <- table(df$admit_type == "Newborn", df$heart_failure)
cat("Contingency table — Newborn vs other × Heart failure:\n")
print(rare_ct)

ft <- fisher.test(rare_ct)
cat(sprintf("\nFisher's exact test: OR=%.3f, p=%.4f\n", unname(ft$estimate), ft$p.value))
cat("→ Use Fisher's exact when any expected cell count < 5\n")
```

```{r}
# ── 4.3  Relative Risk and Odds Ratio ─────────────────────────────────────────
rr_or_correct <- function(exposed, outcome, label = "") {
  a <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 1)
  b <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 0)
  c <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 1)
  d <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 0)
  n_exp <- a + b; n_unexp <- c + d
  risk_e <- a / n_exp; risk_u <- c / n_unexp
  RR <- risk_e / risk_u
  OR <- if (b * c > 0) (a * d) / (b * c) else NA_real_
  se_log_rr <- sqrt((1 - risk_e) / a + (1 - risk_u) / c)
  se_log_or <- sqrt(1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / c + 1 / d)
  rr_lo <- exp(log(RR) - 1.96 * se_log_rr)
  rr_hi <- exp(log(RR) + 1.96 * se_log_rr)
  or_lo <- exp(log(OR) - 1.96 * se_log_or)
  or_hi <- exp(log(OR) + 1.96 * se_log_or)
  cat(sprintf("\n%s\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  RR = %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f–%.2f)\n", RR, rr_lo, rr_hi))
  cat(sprintf("  OR = %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f–%.2f)\n", OR, or_lo, or_hi))
}

rr_or_correct(df$diabetes, df$readmitted_30, "Diabetes → 30-day readmission")
rr_or_correct(df$heart_failure, df$readmitted_30, "Heart failure → 30-day readmission")
```

## 5. Independent Samples & Non-Parametric Tests (Continuous Outcomes)

```{r}
# ── 5.1  LOS by readmission status (non-normal → Mann-Whitney U) ─────────────
g0 <- df$los_days[df$readmitted_30 == 0]
g1 <- df$los_days[df$readmitted_30 == 1]

mw <- wilcox.test(g0, g1, alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE)
# Wilcoxon rank-sum W is the Mann-Whitney U for the first sample
stat_mw <- unname(mw$statistic)
r_rb <- 1 - (2 * stat_mw) / (length(g0) * length(g1))

cat("LOS by 30-day readmission status (Mann-Whitney U)\n")
cat(sprintf("  Not readmitted: median = %.1f days [IQR: %.1f–%.1f]\n",
            median(g0), quantile(g0, 0.25), quantile(g0, 0.75)))
cat(sprintf("  Readmitted    : median = %.1f days [IQR: %.1f–%.1f]\n",
            median(g1), quantile(g1, 0.25), quantile(g1, 0.75)))
cat(sprintf("  U = %.0f, p = %.4f\n", stat_mw, mw$p.value))
cat(sprintf("  Rank-biserial r = %.3f  (|r|>0.1 small, >0.3 medium, >0.5 large)\n", r_rb))
```

```{r}
# ── 5.2  SBP by sex (normal → Welch t-test) ──────────────────────────────────
m_sbp <- df$sbp[df$sex == "M"]
f_sbp <- df$sbp[df$sex == "F"]

# Brown-Forsythe (median-centred Levene) for equal variance
levene_bf <- function(x, g) {
  med <- tapply(x, g, median)
  z <- abs(x - med[as.character(g)])
  summary(aov(z ~ factor(g)))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
}
lev_p <- levene_bf(c(m_sbp, f_sbp), c(rep("M", length(m_sbp)), rep("F", length(f_sbp))))
equal_var <- lev_p > 0.05

tt <- t.test(m_sbp, f_sbp, var.equal = equal_var)
pooled_sd <- sqrt(
  ((length(m_sbp) - 1) * sd(m_sbp)^2 + (length(f_sbp) - 1) * sd(f_sbp)^2) /
    (length(m_sbp) + length(f_sbp) - 2)
)
cohen_d <- (mean(m_sbp) - mean(f_sbp)) / pooled_sd

cat(sprintf("SBP by sex — %s t-test\n", if (!equal_var) "Welch" else "Student"))
cat(sprintf("  Males  : %.1f ± %.1f mmHg\n", mean(m_sbp), sd(m_sbp)))
cat(sprintf("  Females: %.1f ± %.1f mmHg\n", mean(f_sbp), sd(f_sbp)))
cat(sprintf("  Levene p=%.3f → %s\n", lev_p,
            if (!equal_var) "Unequal variances → Welch" else "Equal variances → Student"))
cat(sprintf("  t = %.3f, p = %.4f\n", unname(tt$statistic), tt$p.value))
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's d = %.3f  (|d|<0.2 trivial, <0.5 small, <0.8 medium, ≥0.8 large)\n", cohen_d))
```

## 6. One-Way ANOVA & Post-Hoc Tests

```{r}
# ── 6.1  ANOVA: LOS across payer groups (Kruskal-Wallis — non-normal) ─────────
kw <- kruskal.test(los_days ~ factor(payer), data = df)

cat("LOS across payer groups (Kruskal-Wallis test)\n")
cat(sprintf("H = %.3f, p = %.4f\n\n", unname(kw$statistic), kw$p.value))
cat("Median LOS by payer:\n")
print(
  df |>
    group_by(payer) |>
    summarise(Median = median(los_days), Mean = mean(los_days), N = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(Median)) |>
    mutate(across(c(Median, Mean), ~ round(.x, 1)))
)
```

```{r}
# ── 6.2  ANOVA: Glucose across age groups (normal → one-way ANOVA) ────────────
aov_glu <- aov(glucose ~ age_group, data = df)
aov_sum <- summary(aov_glu)[[1]]
cat(sprintf("Glucose by age group — One-way ANOVA: F=%.3f, p=%.4f\n",
            aov_sum[["F value"]][1], aov_sum[["Pr(>F)"]][1]))

# Post-hoc: Tukey HSD
tukey <- TukeyHSD(aov_glu, conf.level = 0.95)
cat("\nTukey HSD post-hoc comparisons:\n")
print(tukey)
```

## 7. Multiple Comparisons Correction

```{r}
# Test all 10 comorbidities against readmission — naive and corrected
COMORBS <- c("diabetes", "hypertension", "heart_failure", "ckd", "copd",
             "obesity", "afib", "depression", "anxiety", "sleep_apnea")
# Simulate flags for missing comorbidities
set.seed(55)
for (c in c("ckd", "copd", "obesity", "afib", "depression", "anxiety", "sleep_apnea")) {
  if (!c %in% names(df)) df[[c]] <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.15)
}

raw_p <- vapply(COMORBS, function(c) {
  chisq.test(table(df[[c]], df$readmitted_30))$p.value
}, numeric(1))

p_bonf <- p.adjust(raw_p, method = "bonferroni")
p_bh   <- p.adjust(raw_p, method = "BH")
reject_bonf <- p_bonf < 0.05
reject_bh   <- p_bh < 0.05

mc_df <- tibble(
  Comorbidity    = COMORBS,
  `Raw p`        = round(raw_p, 4),
  `Sig (α=0.05)` = raw_p < 0.05,
  `Bonferroni p` = round(p_bonf, 4),
  `Sig (Bonf)`   = reject_bonf,
  `BH FDR p`     = round(p_bh, 4),
  `Sig (BH)`     = reject_bh
)
cat("Multiple comparisons — 10 simultaneous chi-square tests:\n")
print(mc_df)
cat(sprintf("\nWith α=0.05:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Naive:      %d significant\n", sum(raw_p < 0.05)))
cat(sprintf("  Bonferroni: %d significant  (most conservative)\n", sum(reject_bonf)))
cat(sprintf("  BH FDR:     %d significant   (recommended for exploratory analyses)\n", sum(reject_bh)))
```

## 8. Statistical vs Clinical Significance

```{r}
# Power analysis: what N is needed to detect a clinically meaningful difference?
# Two-sided two-sample t-test power (equal n, equal variance)
t_power <- function(d, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  nu  <- 2 * n - 2
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n / 2)
  crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, nu)
  pt(-crit, nu, ncp = ncp) + (1 - pt(crit, nu, ncp = ncp))
}

solve_n_power <- function(d, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80) {
  n <- 10
  while (t_power(d, n, alpha) < power && n < 1e5) n <- n + 1
  n
}

# Scenario: detecting a 1-day mean difference in LOS (SD ≈ 3.5 days)
effect_d <- 1.0 / 3.5   # Cohen's d for 1-day difference
n_needed <- solve_n_power(effect_d, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80)
cat("To detect a 1-day mean LOS difference (SD=3.5 days):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's d = %.3f\n", effect_d))
cat(sprintf("  N per group needed (α=0.05, power=0.80): %d\n", n_needed))

# Panel A: Power vs N for different effect sizes
ns <- seq(20, 500, by = 10)
power_df <- bind_rows(lapply(list(
  list(d = 0.2, label = "d=0.2 (small)",  color = "#93C5FD"),
  list(d = 0.5, label = "d=0.5 (medium)", color = "#2563EB"),
  list(d = 0.8, label = "d=0.8 (large)",  color = "#1E3A8A")
), function(spec) {
  tibble(n = ns, power = vapply(ns, function(n) t_power(spec$d, n), numeric(1)),
         label = spec$label, color = spec$color)
}))

p_a <- ggplot(power_df, aes(n, power, colour = label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, colour = "#DC2626", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("d=0.2 (small)" = "#93C5FD", "d=0.5 (medium)" = "#2563EB",
               "d=0.8 (large)" = "#1E3A8A")
  ) +
  labs(x = "N per group", y = "Statistical power", title = "Power vs sample size",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Panel B: Statistical vs clinical significance illustration
set.seed(7)
ns_sim <- c(50, 200, 500, 2000)
sim_rows <- lapply(ns_sim, function(n) {
  g0s <- rnorm(n, 5.0, 3.5)
  g1s <- rnorm(n, 5.5, 3.5)   # 0.5-day difference (trivial)
  tt  <- t.test(g0s, g1s)
  tibble(n = as.character(n), p = tt$p.value, diff = mean(g1s) - mean(g0s))
})
sim_df <- bind_rows(sim_rows) |>
  mutate(sig = p < 0.05, n = factor(n, levels = as.character(ns_sim)))

p_b <- ggplot(sim_df, aes(n, p, fill = sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, colour = "#DC2626", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("p=%.3f", p)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#DC2626", "FALSE" = "#2563EB"), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Sample size per group", y = "p-value",
    title = "Same 0.5-day LOS difference: p changes with N (clinical significance ≠ statistical significance)"
  )

p_power <- p_a + p_b
print(p_power)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "power_significance.png"), p_power,
       width = 13, height = 5, dpi = 120)

cat("\nKey insight: With N=2000, a trivial 0.5-day LOS difference becomes 'significant'.\n")
cat("Always report effect sizes alongside p-values.\n")
```

       width = 13, height = 5, dpi = 120)

## 9. Knowledge Check
1. Why should you use Mann-Whitney U instead of t-test for LOS comparisons in most health datasets?
2. An OR of 2.1 (95% CI: 1.9–2.3) for diabetes → readmission is statistically significant. Is it clinically meaningful? What else do you need to know?
3. You run 20 chi-square tests comparing comorbidities. How many would you expect to be significant at α=0.05 by chance alone?
4. Bonferroni vs BH FDR: when is each preferred in health research?
5. You find p=0.001 for a 0.3-day LOS difference with N=5,000. Should you change clinical practice?

```{r}
# Exercise 5 — effect size for the 0.3-day LOS example
set.seed(42)
g0_ex <- rnorm(5000, 5.0, 3.5)
g1_ex <- rnorm(5000, 5.3, 3.5)
tt_ex <- t.test(g0_ex, g1_ex)
d_ex  <- (mean(g1_ex) - mean(g0_ex)) / 3.5
cat(sprintf("p = %.4f, Cohen's d = %.3f\n", tt_ex$p.value, d_ex))
cat(sprintf("Difference = %.2f days\n", mean(g1_ex) - mean(g0_ex)))
cat("Cohen's d < 0.2 = trivial effect, regardless of p-value.\n")
```
